explanation: Place one queen in each row, rejecting columns and diagonals already occupied. Backtrack after exploring each safe placement, and copy every complete column sequence into the result.
timeComplexity: O(n × n! + nS), where S is the number of solutions Each valid partial placement tries n columns; set membership is expected constant time. Completed placements each copy n columns.
spaceComplexity: O(n) working space, plus O(nS) output The placement and column/diagonal sets have O(n) entries; output stores n entries per solution.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Before placing a row, the three sets contain exactly the occupied columns and two diagonal identifiers of earlier queens. A candidate absent from all three cannot attack an existing queen. Trying every safe column and undoing it after recursion enumerates every legal placement exactly once.
walkthrough: For n=4, one search branch chooses columns [1,3,0,2]; every row uses a distinct column and diagonal. The other complete branch is [2,0,3,1]. These are the two returned placements.
edgeCases: A placement lists columns in increasing row order.
Boards of size 2 and 3 have no solutions.
Each output placement is copied before backtracking changes the working list.
